description: LangChain-native Python library for structured data extraction from LLMs using Pydantic models, with automatic retry, fallback, and an agentic tool loop.
rules: All extraction functions are async — always use async/await
Use Pydantic v2 models as the schema for extraction
Import from saidex directly — the public API is fully exposed in saidex.__init__
Use extract_data_from_text for simple text input, extract_data for chat history or multimodal content
Use ExtractionMode.JSON for models that do not support tool calling

When a provider is behind an OpenAI-compatible gateway (Kimi/Moonshot, Qwen, DeepSeek) that rejects strict / forced tool_choice / parallel_tool_calls with an HTTP 400, pass tool_config=ToolCallConfig.COMPATIBLE — SAIDEX also relaxes those flags automatically once per attempt (disable with ToolCallConfig(auto_relax=False))
To reject hallucinated values, mark fields with Grounded() (Annotated marker) or GroundedField() so the extracted value is verified against the source text

Pass LangChain callback handlers via callbacks= to trace runs: each extraction becomes one chain-run span with nested LLM generations and, in the agent loop, per-tool spans; enable capture_source_text=True only if exporting the input text to the tracing backend is acceptable

In LangGraph agents, use saidex.langgraph.SaidexToolNode (extra: saidex[langgraph]) as a drop-in for langgraph.prebuilt.ToolNode — it repairs invalid_tool_calls and validates args before execution; without correction_model the agent fixes invalid calls from structured feedback, with correction_model=llm SAIDEX corrects them inside the node and the correction never enters graph state; on_unresolved='feedback'|'raise'|hook(UnresolvedToolCall) decides what happens to calls that stay invalid; validators={tool_name: fn(args, ctx)} adds per-tool checks with a saidex.ToolCallValidatorContext; on_invalid is deprecated

To enforce business rules after Pydantic validation, pass validator= to any extract_data* function; return None to accept, a str to reject, or a list of str and/or saidex.ValidationIssue(message, field_path=..., error_type=..., on_mismatch='retry'|'flag') to report several per-field findings — 'flag' issues are recorded in stats.field_issues without consuming a retry

stats.failure_reason is a saidex.FailureReason StrEnum (validation_exhausted, parse_error, llm_error, no_tool_call) or None on success; it describes only the last attempt, and comparing it with the plain string still works

To make an external validator depend on the retry round, wrap it with saidex.with_context(fn); fn(instance, ctx) receives a saidex.ValidatorContext(attempt, max_attempts, is_final, model_label, is_fallback) — is_final is true only on the last attempt of the whole run, so returning on_mismatch='flag' there accepts the instance

When an extraction fails, stats.last_candidate holds the most recent schema-valid instance rejected by grounding or the external validator (a list for extract_data_list), and stats.last_rejection the retry-level FieldIssues that rejected it; both are empty on a clean success (a run salvaged by on_exhausted keeps them) and the candidate may contain PII

To keep a partial result when retries run out, pass on_exhausted=fn to any extract_data*/agent function; fn(last_candidate, last_rejection) returns the instance to keep (a list for extract_data_list) or None — the run then succeeds with stats.salvaged=True; the hook gets a copy and its result is re-validated against the schema only (a list hook must return item schema instances); use saidex.issue_item_index(issue, list_field) to map issue paths like 'items -> 3 -> quote' to item indexes

When stats.failure_reason is 'llm_error', stats.llm_error_kind (saidex.ModelErrorKind: rate_limit, timeout, connection, server_error, authentication, permission_denied, invalid_request, not_found, context_overflow, other) says why, provider-independently; saidex.classify_model_error(exc) does the same mapping for your own handling

Pass reasoning_escalation=['low', 'medium', 'high'] (or True for the model profile's levels) to any extract_data*/agent function to bind reasoning_effort per attempt, escalating on each retry; the fallback model only escalates with fallback_reasoning_escalation; stats.reasoning_effort and ValidatorContext.reasoning_effort show the level; needs an integration that accepts reasoning_effort (ChatOpenAI, recent ChatAnthropic; not ChatOllama) or the run fails with llm_error_kind invalid_request

Use field: X | MISSING = MISSING (pydantic >= 2.14) for values that may be absent from the source; the model omits the key (null is rejected) and results drop it on dump; put Grounded() via field_check(...) or Annotated[X | MISSING, Grounded()], not GroundedStr | MISSING
